references.text: All the nations came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was severe over all the earth, which shows the extent of the famine and Joseph's role as provider.
Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt and sent his sons there to buy some, reflecting the response to the famine mentioned in Genesis 41:55.
There was no food in the whole region because the famine was very severe, which underscores the severity of the famine that led the people to cry out to Pharaoh for bread.
Joseph's advice to Pharaoh to gather grain during the good years explains why Pharaoh sent the people to Joseph—it was Joseph who had planned the grain storage.

Mary said to the servants at the wedding in Cana: 'Do whatever he tells you.' These words mirror Pharaoh's words about Joseph: 'Do whatever he tells you'—a classic typological parallel between Joseph and Jesus.
Direct continuation: The appointment in 41:41 creates the authority that saves Egypt in 41:55.
Narrative context: 41:55 is the start of the crisis where the people turn to Joseph, while 47:20 shows the end where the land becomes Pharaoh's property.
